articles.title: Trends of radiotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma in the Republic of Korea: a national cohort, 2013-2021
articles.summary: This study analyzes the expansion of radiotherapy in the management of hepatocellular carcinoma, noting that while it has become a core component of multidisciplinary care, utilization remains geographically centralized. These findings highlight ongoing challenges in equitable access to radiation oncology infrastructure.

articles.title: Dosimetric impact of target volume anatomical parameters on radiotherapy after right-sided breast-conserving surgery
articles.summary: Researchers identified exploratory observational thresholds for target volume parameters associated with increased heart and lung dose risks in breast-conserving radiotherapy. The study emphasizes the need for prospective validation of these thresholds to improve clinical risk stratification and minimize radiation exposure to organs at risk.

articles.title: Gamification of clinical decision-making for medical physics residents
articles.summary: This article describes a new lecture series utilizing gamified clinical scenarios to support medical physics residency training. The framework covers essential topics such as patient safety, quality assurance, and treatment planning to enhance trainee clinical reasoning skills.

articles.title: Outcomes of Proton Beam Therapy in Infants and Very Young Children
articles.summary: This study evaluates proton beam therapy outcomes in children aged three years or younger within a national treatment pathway. The findings underscore the necessity of biology-guided patient selection, age-appropriate organ-at-risk dose constraints, and rigorous long-term surveillance.

articles.title: A novel deep learning segmentation and multimodal radiomics approach for radiation proctitis prediction in cervical cancer
articles.summary: This study introduces an AI-based framework that integrates deep learning segmentation with multimodal radiomics to predict radiation proctitis. The model aims to improve the accuracy of treatment planning and reduce complications in cervical cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.

articles.title: Pre-treatment T2WI-based automated artificial intelligence system for predicting neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy response and prognosis in locally advanced rectal cancer: a multicenter study
articles.summary: Researchers developed and externally validated an AI system using T2-weighted MRI to predict responses to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer. The tool is intended to serve as a decision-support resource to assist clinicians in prognostic stratification.

articles.title: Deep learning-based self-supervised detection and localization of magnetic resonance imaging anomalies in artificial intelligence-supported radiotherapy workflows
articles.summary: Researchers developed self-supervised anomaly-detection frameworks for pelvic MRI to improve the reliability of AI-supported radiotherapy workflows. The study addresses the challenge of out-of-distribution image data, which can introduce errors in automated clinical tasks.

articles.title: Mid-trial dosimetric analysis of the korean radiation oncology group 19 - 09 multi-institutional prospective cohort study on breast cancer
articles.summary: A mid-trial dosimetric analysis revealed significant dose deviations in breast cancer radiotherapy, suggesting that current methods for assessing regional nodal irradiation (RNI) omission may be inadequate. Future analysis will focus on correlating specific nodal doses with long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Neurocognitive function and quality of life results from a phase II study (NRG/RTOG 0424) of temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy regimen for high-risk low-grade gliomas
articles.summary: This phase II study evaluated the long-term neurocognitive and quality of life impacts of temozolomide-based chemoradiotherapy for high-risk low-grade gliomas. Findings indicate a notable decline in neurocognitive function during the first year post-treatment, highlighting the importance of integrated monitoring to inform future clinical decisions.

articles.title: Dose-rate metrics for ionization-chamber recombination in synchrotron-based ultra-high-dose-rate proton and carbon-ion beams
articles.summary: This research assesses the validity of quasi-static response models for predicting ionization-chamber recombination in ultra-high-dose-rate particle beams. It compares various dose-rate metrics to better define saturation correction factors in synchrotron-based delivery systems.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of plan robustness in proton and photon radiotherapy in deep inspiration breath-hold for mediastinal lymphomas
articles.summary: Researchers compared the robustness of proton pencil beam scanning and VMAT for treating mediastinal lymphomas. While both were found to be robust, proton therapy demonstrated superior organ-at-risk sparing.

articles.title: Preliminary Dose Constraints for Testing Intensity Modulated Proton Therapy in Anal Cancer Trials
articles.summary: This study establishes preliminary dose constraints for intensity modulated proton therapy in anal cancer. These guidelines aim to facilitate future clinical trials by optimizing target coverage and reducing dose to organs at risk.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: BayCare Health System has successfully treated its first patient at the new St. Joseph's Hospital proton therapy center. The facility utilizes the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie upright patient positioning solution.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: The BayCare Proton Center has successfully initiated patient treatments using the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie solution. This facility represents a new implementation of compact proton therapy technology.

articles.title: 50 million Americans live in counties without a radiation oncology clinic, study finds
articles.summary: A recent study highlights that 50 million Americans reside in counties lacking a radiation oncology clinic, underscoring significant geographic disparities in access to cancer care. The findings emphasize the ongoing challenges in providing equitable radiation treatment coverage across the United States.

articles.title: ASTRO updates guideline on shorter-course radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer
articles.summary: The American Society for Radiation Oncology has released updated clinical guidelines recommending the use of shorter-course radiation therapy regimens for patients with localized prostate cancer. These evidence-based updates aim to standardize care and improve efficiency for patients undergoing radiation treatment.

articles.title: IBA treats first patient in clinical trial of FLASH proton therapy for head and neck cancer
articles.summary: IBA has announced the treatment of the first patient in the C-FLASH-01 clinical trial, evaluating the safety and efficacy of ConformalFLASH proton therapy. This trial marks a significant milestone in testing ultra-high dose rate radiation delivery for head and neck cancer patients.

articles.title: Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute opens new wellness space
articles.summary: The Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute has inaugurated a new wellness facility dedicated to supporting patients and their caregivers. This regional development enhances the supportive care infrastructure at this key proton therapy center in the DMV area.
